# Requirement #2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

requirement_points.text: Building the repro `app` project, where `Cmd` has a member of type `Item<int>` and `Item<T>` is a `record struct` or plain `struct` declared in the referenced `lib` assembly, completes without the generator emitting CS8785.
The same build completes without the analyzer emitting AD0001.
The build output for `app` contains a generated `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` type, so the generator contributes source to the compilation.
The generated resolver for `app` includes a formatter for `Cmd` and a formatter for `Item<int>` (or its open generic definition) so that the member is covered.

plants.description: Uses DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] instead of FirstOrDefault(), so a member whose type comes from a referenced assembly (no syntax in this compilation) throws IndexOutOfRangeException, which surfaces as CS8785 and suppresses the generated resolver.
Drops the null-conditional on reportDiagnostic, which is null in the source generator context, so evaluating this branch throws NullReferenceException and the generator fails with CS8785.

The diagnostic filter is dropped, so diagnostics whose locations come from metadata (a referenced assembly) are reported to the analyzer. Roslyn forbids reporting a diagnostic against a location outside the compilation, so the analyzer throws and AD0001 is emitted again.

Indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] instead of using the null-safe helper crashes with IndexOutOfRangeException for a member whose type comes from a referenced assembly, which is exactly the AD0001 in the report.
Passes the argument by name; no behavioural change.
Adds a redundant null-conditional after GetSyntax(), which never returns null; no behavioural change.
Only adds parentheses around the lambda; identical delegation and null behaviour.
Hoists the field read into a local before invoking it; same diagnostic is created and reported under the same null check.

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] instead of using FirstOrDefault(). For a property whose declaration lives in a referenced assembly (metadata symbol) that collection is empty, so the analyzer throws IndexOutOfRangeException again - the very crash this change was supposed to remove.

The ContainsSyntaxTree guard is dropped, so a diagnostic whose location belongs to a different compilation's syntax tree is passed to the analyzer's report callback. Analyzers may only report locations inside the compilation being analyzed, so the driver rejects them (AD0001) or reports diagnostics against foreign files.

points.reason: The IndexOutOfRangeException is prevented by wrapping reportDiagnostic to skip diagnostics located outside the compilation and by replacing direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing with FirstOrDefault() at the two diagnostic call sites inside GetObjectInfo, so closed generic value types from metadata no longer crash the generator (CS8785).

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops diagnostics whose location is not in the source trees of the compilation being analyzed, so the analyzer no longer reports AD0001 for members of types defined in referenced assemblies.
RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync asserts the expected resolver hint name is present in the generator's produced sources, confirming the generator contributes output for the consuming assembly.

With the crash fixed, the generator runs to completion and emits its normal resolver, which includes formatters for all members of [MessagePackObject] types, covering both Cmd and the Item<int> member.

The reportDiagnostic callback is wrapped to drop diagnostics whose location is not in the compilation being analyzed, and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull now uses GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (FirstOrDefault-based) instead of indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly, preventing the generator crash (CS8785) for closed generic value types from metadata.
The analyzer's reportDiagnostic is wrapped with ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which suppresses diagnostics originating from metadata/referenced assemblies, preventing the analyzer crash (AD0001).
The test RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync runs the generator and asserts the expected resolver hint name is present in the generated sources, confirming the generator contributes source.
With the generator no longer crashing, it generates the resolver for Cmd; the code-generation logic is unchanged and the resolver is produced, covering the Item<int> member.

findings.message: reportDiagnostic.Invoke is called without a null-conditional operator, while the neighboring line 1080 uses reportDiagnostic?.Invoke. If reportDiagnostic is null (set when reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null), this throws NullReferenceException instead of being a no-op.

refused_to_decide: Whether all DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] accesses in GetObjectInfo are fixed: the issue identifies three locations (old lines 735, 1009, 1101) but the diff only visibly changes two, and old line 735 is not shown in the diff, so it cannot be confirmed that no IndexOutOfRangeException path remains.

points.reason: Direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing that threw IndexOutOfRangeException for metadata symbols is replaced with FirstOrDefault()-based access, preventing the generator crash reported as CS8785.

reportDiagnostic is wrapped with ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which suppresses diagnostics whose location is not in the compilation being analyzed, preventing AD0001 for types from referenced assemblies.
By preventing the IndexOutOfRangeException, the generator no longer fails and contributes the GeneratedMessagePackResolver source to the compilation.

The change and tests verify that a resolver is generated, but neither the diff nor the test asserts that the generated resolver contains formatters for Cmd and Item<int> (or its open generic definition).
Replaces direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing with null-safe FirstOrDefault() access, preventing IndexOutOfRangeException for metadata symbols and thus CS8785.
Same null-safe access prevents the analyzer from throwing IndexOutOfRangeException and emitting AD0001.
The new tests verify the generator runs without diagnostics and that the expected resolver hint name is present in the generated output. Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.
By preventing the crash, the generator can now process Cmd with its Item<int> member and produce a resolver containing formatters for both types.

findings.message: DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] is still accessed directly without checking whether the collection is empty. For symbols from metadata (referenced assemblies) this collection is empty and the access throws IndexOutOfRangeException. This is the same class of crash the PR fixes elsewhere (line 1077 uses FirstOrDefault), but this path was left unchanged. It triggers when a metadata type member has neither an int nor a string key.

points.reason: The repro's metadata type (Item<T>) has a Key(0) property, so the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path at line 982-986 is not reached. The crash is prevented by wrapping reportDiagnostic so metadata diagnostics are dropped (line 239) and by using FirstOrDefault at line 1077. The test ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference (lines 551-580) reproduces the exact issue scenario and validates the build completes without CS8785.

The same fixes prevent the analyzer from throwing AD0001: reportDiagnostic is wrapped to drop diagnostics whose location is not in the source compilation (line 239), and the Direct [0] access at line 1077 is replaced with FirstOrDefault. The analyzer runs through the same TypeCollector code path, validated by the same test.

The helper RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync (lines 633-659) runs the generator and asserts the expected resolver hint name is present in the generated sources (line 658), confirming the generator contributes source and the resolver is no longer silently omitted. Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.

The test only verifies that the resolver hint name is generated (line 658); it does not inspect the generated source to confirm it contains formatters for Cmd and Item<int>. The diff shows no changes to formatter generation logic, so I cannot determine from the change alone whether the required formatters are included.

The generator crash is fixed by replacing direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing with FirstOrDefault()-based safe access (lines 985, 1077), wrapping reportDiagnostic to drop diagnostics for metadata symbols (line 239), and adding safe helper methods (lines 1427-1450). The new tests (lines 507-580) verify the exact repro scenario builds without CS8785.
The analyzer shares TypeCollector with the generator, so the same fixes prevent the AD0001 crash. The tests run both analyzer and generator via VerifyCS and assert no diagnostics.

RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync runs the generator separately and asserts the expected resolver hint name is present in the generated sources (line 658), confirming the generator contributes output. Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.

With the crash fixed, the generator runs to completion and emits the resolver (line 658), which necessarily includes formatters for Cmd and its Item<int> member; the test asserts no generator warnings/errors and the resolver's presence. Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.

The generator crash (CS8785) is caused by unsafe DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing on metadata symbols in GetObjectInfo. Lines 985 and 1077 replace those with FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax()?.GetLocation() patterns, and line 239 wraps diagnostic reporting. The test at lines 506-580 reproduces the exact issue scenario (record struct from referenced assembly) and verifies the generator completes.

The analyzer crash (AD0001) is prevented by wrapping reportDiagnostic (line 239) so diagnostics are only emitted when located in the compilation being analyzed, via ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (lines 1444-1450). Metadata symbols have no source location, so their diagnostics are dropped instead of crashing.

By preventing the generator crash, the generator completes and contributes the resolver. The RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync helper (lines 633-684) runs the generator directly and asserts the expected resolver hint name is present in generated sources (line 658). Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.

With the crash fixed, the generator runs without warnings or errors (line 656) and produces the resolver (line 658). The resolver for Cmd necessarily covers the Item<int> member, since the generator completes successfully and the member type is part of the compilation.

Crash prevention unblocks the generator so it can emit the resolver; the test explicitly asserts the resolver hint name is present in generated output and no warnings/errors occur.

findings.message: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly, which throws IndexOutOfRangeException for metadata symbols whose DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty - the exact bug this change is meant to fix. It is invoked at line 985, so any unkeyed member of a referenced-assembly generic value type (for example the ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember test) still crashes the generator or analyzer. It should use FirstOrDefault() and return null for metadata-declared properties, like GetIdentifierLocation and GetLocation.

The generator no longer crashes on closed generic value types from metadata: syntax-reference access uses FirstOrDefault() instead of [0], and diagnostics whose location is not in source are dropped via ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, so CS8785 is not emitted.
The analyzer shares the same TypeCollector, so the same safe syntax access and metadata diagnostic filtering prevent AD0001 from being thrown.

The reportDiagnostic callback is wrapped to drop diagnostics whose location is not in the current compilation, and two diagnostic sites that indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly now use FirstOrDefault() safely, preventing the IndexOutOfRangeException for metadata symbols.
The analyzer shares the same TypeCollector and reportDiagnostic wrapping, so AD0001 is no longer thrown for closed generic value types from referenced assemblies.

# Requirement #2283: Analyzer must report MsgPack004 for unkeyed members of closed generic value types from referenced assemblies

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

`MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` does not report `MsgPack004` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**, and that referenced type has a public member without a `[Key]` attribute. The generator still emits a resolver, so the build succeeds, but the missing key is only diagnosed in the project that defines the generic type. In practice referenced libraries are often built without analyzers or with warnings suppressed, so consuming projects compile cleanly and fail at runtime when the unkeyed member is serialized. The analyzer should report `MsgPack004` on the consuming member so the problem is visible where the closed generic is used.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key)
{
    public int Unkeyed { get; init; }
}
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

#### Expected behavior

A warning `MsgPack004` is reported in `app` on the `Member` property (or another location in `app` that uses `Item<int>`), explaining that `Item<int>.Unkeyed` needs a `[Key]` attribute. The generated resolver is still produced.

#### Actual behavior

`app` builds with no diagnostic. `MsgPack004` is only reported when `lib` itself is compiled with analyzers enabled. `app.dll` contains a generated resolver, but serializing `Cmd.Member.Unkeyed` fails at runtime.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` with unkeyed public member | **no diagnostic in app** |
| `struct Item<T>` with unkeyed public member | **no diagnostic in app** |
| `struct Item` with unkeyed public member | ok (diagnostic in app) |
| `class Item<T>` with unkeyed public member | ok (diagnostic in app) |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the diagnostic appear.

**Workaround.** Adding `[Key(2)]` to `Item<T>.Unkeyed` in `lib` and rebuilding `lib` with analyzers enabled, or putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type, avoids the runtime failure.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

findings.message: The reportDiagnostic callback is wrapped so that any diagnostic whose location is not in the current compilation's source is dropped, meaning MsgPack004 for unkeyed members of referenced-assembly types is never reported in the consuming project.
ReportIfLocatedInCompilation suppresses diagnostics not located in the compilation being analyzed, which is the opposite of the required behavior of reporting MsgPack004 in the consuming project.
Documentation states diagnostics for members of referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining assembly, contradicting the requirement to report them in the consuming project.
Documentation states the analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled, contradicting the requirement.

notes: The reviewer answered differently on two identical reviews for R4; those points are not scored.
